annotation.title_clean: The Dawn of the AI Robots: Towards a New Framework of AI Robot Accountability
annotation.title_en: The Dawn of the AI Robots: Towards a New Framework of AI Robot Accountability
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tóth, Z.; Caruana, R.; Gruber, T.; Loebbecke, C.
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual business-ethics paper proposing a framework for AI robot accountability. It combines locus of morality (human to AI agency) and moral intensity to derive four 'accountability clusters' (illegal, immoral, permissible, supererogatory), showing accountability dispersing across designers, users, industry, governments and intergovernmental regimes.
key_provisions_or_claims: Business ethics literature neglects AI robots such as driverless cars, care robots and lethal autonomous weapons.
Framework links locus of morality and moral intensity to accountability.
Accountability becomes widely dispersed as AI agency and moral intensity escalate.
Four categorical responses: illegal, immoral, permissible, supererogatory.
Offers consideration points for regulators on AI robot learning behaviour and decision-making.
